request.description: A fragment of a long dungeon wall, seen straight on from the front, filling the frame with no centre and no edges of its own — every course and every member runs off the sides of the frame and continues beyond it. Cold blue-grey quarried stone in level courses. The blocks are different lengths, some short and some long, and one course sits a pixel lower than the rest. Two or three stones have a corner knocked off. The mortar joints are much darker than the stone faces, about a third of their brightness, and each stone carries a single lighter pixel line along its upper edge so the courses separate at a glance. Running horizontally straight off both the left and right edges of the frame is a squared timber baulk, thick enough to have two visible faces: a flat front and a darker under-edge where it stands off the wall. It is held by two driven iron pins with visible flat heads, and the stone around each pin is bruised dark where it was hammered home. Along the top edge, a band three or four pixels deep of the wall's upper surface, one flat value clearly lighter than the front face, meeting the front on a single hard line. Nothing is green and nothing is warm. Heavy, over-built and plain.
